questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.1 Recognize common construction fall hazards
questions.text: Which condition is a common fall hazard on a construction site?

answers.text: An unprotected floor opening in an active work area
A marked walkway kept clear of stored material
A properly installed guardrail around a platform
A secured ladder used according to instructions

explanations.a: Unprotected openings can expose workers to serious or fatal falls. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: a clear marked walkway reduces trip and access hazards.
explanations.c: A guardrail is a fall prevention control.
explanations.d: Correct ladder use reduces fall exposure.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.1 Recognize common construction fall hazards
questions.text: A worker is carrying materials near an unguarded roof edge. What is the main hazard?

answers.text: Heat stress from outdoor work
A fall from elevation
Chemical exposure from stored materials
Noise exposure from nearby equipment

explanations.a: Heat stress may need control, but the edge hazard creates immediate fall exposure.
explanations.b: Unguarded edges expose workers to falls, especially when carrying materials limits balance and visibility. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: The scenario does not describe chemical handling or exposure.
explanations.d: Noise may be present, but the unguarded edge creates the main fall hazard.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.1 Recognize common construction fall hazards
questions.text: During fall hazard planning on a construction site, what makes a surface a fall concern?

answers.text: It has a supervisor assigned to the crew
It has a toolbox nearby but no elevation change
It is elevated, unstable, slippery, incomplete, or near an unprotected edge or opening
It is located inside the project trailer

explanations.a: Supervision helps, but it does not define whether the surface has fall exposure.
explanations.b: A toolbox alone does not create the same fall exposure as an opening or edge.
explanations.c: Fall hazards arise when surfaces or nearby openings can allow a worker to lose balance or fall. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: An indoor location is not automatically a fall hazard without an exposure.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.2 Identify fall prevention and protection systems
questions.text: Which practice supports fall restraint?

answers.text: Climbing with tools in both hands
Allowing the worker to fall and then stopping the fall
Using a system that prevents the worker from reaching the fall hazard
Standing near an opening without a tie-off point

explanations.a: Prevention focus: climbing with both hands full increases fall risk.
explanations.b: Construction context: that describes fall arrest rather than restraint.
explanations.c: Fall restraint prevents the worker from reaching an edge or opening where a fall could occur. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: standing near an opening without control leaves the hazard unmanaged.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.2 Identify fall prevention and protection systems
questions.text: Which action best addresses fall prevention and protection systems? Which control prevents workers from reaching a fall edge?

answers.text: A warning shouted after the worker reaches the edge
A toolbox talk with no physical control
A harness with no anchor point
A properly installed guardrail system

explanations.a: A warning after exposure does not physically prevent a fall.
explanations.b: Training helps but does not replace required protection at serious fall hazards.
explanations.c: A harness without a proper anchorage is not an effective fall protection system.
explanations.d: Guardrails are fall prevention systems that create a physical barrier at edges or openings. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.2 Identify fall prevention and protection systems
questions.text: What is the purpose of a personal fall arrest system?

answers.text: To stop a worker after a fall begins while limiting the forces on the worker
To replace the need for anchorage and inspection
To make rescue planning unnecessary
To keep all workers away from the edge without other controls

explanations.a: Personal fall arrest systems are designed to arrest a fall and reduce injury when properly designed and used. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Anchorage and inspection are essential parts of fall arrest protection.
explanations.c: A fall arrest system increases the need for rescue planning after a fall.
explanations.d: Keeping workers away from edges is a prevention function, not fall arrest.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.2 Identify fall prevention and protection systems
questions.text: Which item is part of a complete personal fall arrest system?

answers.text: A ladder label and a tool belt
Full-body harness, connector, and suitable anchorage
Hard hat, gloves, and safety glasses
Warning tape alone around the work zone

explanations.a: Construction context: labels and tool belts do not arrest falls.
explanations.b: A complete personal fall arrest system includes compatible components such as a harness, connector, and anchorage. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: these are PPE items, but they do not form a fall arrest system.
explanations.d: Warning tape alone does not create a complete fall arrest system.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.3 Recognize safe practices for scaffolds, ladders, and aerial work surfaces
questions.text: A worker on a mobile scaffold needs to move it. What should happen first?

answers.text: Push the scaffold quickly to reduce time at height
Ask workers to hold nearby piping for balance
Workers should get off the scaffold unless the equipment and procedure allow safe movement with occupants
Move it over debris if the wheels are large

explanations.a: Fast movement can increase instability and fall risk.
explanations.b: Using piping for balance is not a safe movement method.
explanations.c: Moving elevated platforms with workers on them can create falls unless strict safe conditions are met. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Debris can make movement unstable and should be cleared.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.3 Recognize safe practices for scaffolds, ladders, and aerial work surfaces
questions.text: Which aerial lift practice reduces fall risk?

answers.text: Use boxes on the platform to gain extra height
Tie off to a nearby structure when it conflicts with safe lift use
Climb onto the midrail to reach higher work
Stand on the platform floor and use required fall protection according to equipment instructions

explanations.a: Improvised height increases instability and fall risk.
explanations.b: Prevention focus: tie-off must follow equipment and site requirements and not create additional hazards.
explanations.c: Construction context: climbing rails increases fall exposure.
explanations.d: Workers should remain on the platform floor and follow fall protection requirements for the lift. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.3 Recognize safe practices for scaffolds, ladders, and aerial work surfaces
questions.text: During fall hazard planning on a construction site, what is a safe ladder practice?

answers.text: Maintain three points of contact when climbing where feasible
Place a ladder on loose debris to gain height
Carry bulky materials in both hands while climbing
Use the top step of a stepladder as a work platform

explanations.a: Three points of contact help maintain stability during ladder climbing. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Unstable bases can cause ladder movement and falls.
explanations.c: Carrying bulky materials can prevent stable climbing.
explanations.d: Top steps are not intended for standing unless the ladder is designed for that use.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.3 Recognize safe practices for scaffolds, ladders, and aerial work surfaces
questions.text: Which scaffold condition should be corrected before use?

answers.text: Tagged scaffold inspected and released for use
Missing guardrails on an elevated scaffold platform where fall protection is required
Planks properly installed and secured
Access provided by a safe ladder or stair tower

explanations.a: Inspection and release support safe use.
explanations.b: Missing guardrails can expose scaffold users to falls and should be corrected before use. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Properly installed planks reduce fall and collapse hazards.
explanations.d: Safe access reduces climbing and fall hazards.

questions.text: During training, which scaffold condition should be corrected before use?

During the shift, missing guardrails on an elevated scaffold platform where fall protection is required
During the shift, tagged scaffold inspected and released for use
During the shift, planks properly installed and secured

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls

questions.text: During fall hazard planning on a construction site, A worker on a mobile scaffold needs to move it. What should happen first?

answers.text: On the project, push the scaffold quickly to reduce time at height
On the project, ask workers to hold nearby piping for balance
On the project, workers should get off the scaffold unless the equipment and procedure allow safe movement with occupants
On the project, move it over debris if the wheels are large

explanations.a: Fast movement can increase instability and fall risk.

explanations.c: Moving elevated platforms with workers on them can create falls unless strict safe conditions are met. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Debris can make movement unstable and should be cleared.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.3 Recognize safe practices for scaffolds, ladders, and aerial work surfaces
questions.text: During training, which aerial lift practice reduces fall risk?

answers.text: On the project, use boxes on the platform to gain extra height
On the project, tie off to a nearby structure when it conflicts with safe lift use
On the project, climb onto the midrail to reach higher work
On the project, stand on the platform floor and use required fall protection according to equipment instructions

explanations.a: Answer boundary: improvised height increases instability and fall risk.

explanations.c: Climbing rails increases fall exposure.
explanations.d: Workers should remain on the platform floor and follow fall protection requirements for the lift. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.4 Identify controls for floor openings, edges, roofs, and excavations
questions.text: What should be done with a floor hole in a work area?

answers.text: Cover it securely or guard it so workers are protected from falling through
Place loose cardboard over it
Mark it mentally during the morning briefing
Leave it uncovered until the end of the shift

explanations.a: Floor holes need covers or guarding that prevent workers from falling through or into them. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A weak or unsecured cover can fail and create a hidden hazard.
explanations.c: Memory is not a reliable control for an open hole.
explanations.d: Exposure should be controlled before workers are near the hole.

questions.text: For a recent task, a supervisor is reviewing Focus Four fall hazards. Which action should occur before using a harness and lanyard?

answers.text: Use damaged equipment for short tasks
Assume equipment is safe because it was used yesterday
Inspect the equipment for damage, wear, labels, and compatibility
Tie knots in the lanyard to shorten it without review

explanations.b: Pre-use inspection is still needed.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.5 Recognize planning, training, inspection, and rescue considerations for fall protection

questions.text: Why is rescue planning important for personal fall arrest systems?

answers.text: A fallen worker can always climb back without help
The system prevents every fall from occurring
Rescue planning replaces equipment inspection
A suspended worker may need prompt rescue after a fall is arrested

explanations.a: A worker may be injured, suspended, or unable to self-rescue.
explanations.b: Fall arrest stops a fall after it begins rather than preventing exposure.
explanations.c: Rescue planning and inspection are both needed.
explanations.d: Fall arrest can leave a worker suspended, making rescue planning a critical part of protection. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Focus Four: Falls
questions.objective: 3.5 Recognize planning, training, inspection, and rescue considerations for fall protection

questions.text: Why should fall protection be planned before work at height begins?

answers.text: Controls, equipment, anchor points, access, and rescue can be arranged before exposure
Planning is useful only after the first fall occurs
Workers can improvise anchors once they reach the edge
Rescue can always wait until emergency responders arrive

explanations.a: Planning before exposure helps ensure fall protection is available, suitable, and usable. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: planning should prevent incidents rather than react to them.
explanations.c: Improvised anchors can fail and should not replace planned anchorage.
explanations.d: Suspended workers may need prompt rescue planning.
